topic.title: Why can't you drive from North to South America?
topic.map_answer: the one gap in the highway's line: about 106 km between Yaviza in Panama and Turbo in Colombia, where the Darién rainforest and the Atrato marshes sit across the border

shape.name: The missing link
shape.beats: hook: one road drawn down two continents and the question -> how long it is against something the viewer can feel -> a car drives it south from Alaska, the counter climbing, country after country -> the line stops dead in Panama, how short the gap is -> what fills the gap on the map: rainforest, mountains, the swamp -> the bridges and plans that never closed it -> the turn: the gap is kept open on purpose, a park and a disease barrier -> payoff: the one thing the gap keeps out -> loop back to the road
shape.why: a why-shaped story whose answer is one gap in one line on the map, found by driving the line end to end until it stops

title: Why does the road from Alaska to Argentina stop in Panama?
description:
One road runs from Alaska to Argentina. Why does it stop dead in Panama?
The Darién Gap, found on the map by driving the Pan-American Highway south until the tarmac runs out.
Sources: Wikipedia, Darién Gap (Nov 2026). The characters are not advisers.
